chunks: Whoever mentions the Name of Allah, Exalted is He, over his wudu (ablution), it is as though he has performed ghusl (ritual bath).

2. And al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Abān, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from some of our companions, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
When you pronounce the Name in wudu (ablution), your whole body becomes pure; and when you do not pronounce it, nothing of your body becomes pure except what the water passes over.

3. And with this isnad, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn al-Walīd, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Dāwūd al-ʿAjalī, the mawlā of Abū al-Maghrāʾ, from Abū Baṣīr, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said:

O Abā Muḥammad, whoever performs wudu (ablution) and mentions the Name of Allah, his entire body becomes pure; and whoever does not pronounce it, nothing of his body becomes pure except what the water reaches.
4. As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from some of his companions, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

A man performed wudu (ablution) and prayed, so the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said to him: Repeat your prayer and your wudu (ablution). So he did so, and he performed wudu (ablution) and prayed. Then the Prophet عليه السلام said to him: Repeat your wudu (ablution) and your prayer. So he did so, and he performed wudu (ablution) and prayed. Then the Prophet عليه السلام said to him: Repeat your wudu (ablution) and your prayer. Then he came to أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام and complained of that to him. He said: Did you pronounce the Name when you performed wudu (ablution)? He said: No. He said: Pronounce it over your wudu (ablution). So he pronounced it and prayed. Then he came to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and he did not command him to repeat.

So the proper way regarding this report is that we understand the naming therein as referring to the niyyah (intention), whose obligation is established. As for other utterances besides that, they are only recommended, not obligatory as a fixed duty. This is indicated by his statement عليه السلام in the first two reports: whoever does not pronounce it, only that part of his body over which the water passes becomes pure. If it had been obligatory, then whoever abandoned it, nothing of his body would have become pure in any state, because he would not have become purified.

key_terms.وُضُوئِهِ: his wudu (ablution), the ritual washing before salat
key_terms.ٱسْمَ ٱللَّهِ: the Name of Allah, invoked during the act of purification
key_terms.ٱلتَّسْمِيَةَ: the pronouncing of the Name of Allah
key_terms.ٱلنِّيَّةِ: intention, the inward resolve connected to the act

ai.seo_question: Is saying the Name of Allah during wudu (ablution) obligatory or recommended in Shiʿi hadith?
ai.summary: These reports discuss mentioning the Name of Allah during wudu (ablution) and its effect on purity. The concluding legal clarification explains that the wording about tasmiyah is understood in light of niyyah (intention) as obligatory, while verbal mention itself is recommended rather than obligatory.
